newsitem.title: CANADA: Hydro-Quebec to open power grid to other producers.
newsitem.headline: Hydro-Quebec to open power grid to other producers.

text.p: The Quebec government said on Tuesday that it plans to open Hydro-Quebec's power grid to electricity producers in the other Canadian provinces and the United States.

The government said it plans to create a new energy agency that will examine a number of policy initiatives, including allowing other Canadian and U.S. electricity producers to use Hydro-Quebec's power grid to transport electricity to customers.
"In permitting access to Hydro-Quebec's transportation network, the government wants to facilitate the realization of new energy projects," Quebec energy minister Guy Chevrette said in a statement.

The initiative is part of sweeping changes proposed by the Quebec government, which also plans to allow the private sector to have a greater role in the production of electricity in the Canadian province. Quebec government-owned Hydro-Quebec currently generates, distributes and markets most of the electricity produced in the province.
But the government said it has no plans to privatize Hydro-Quebec, which was created in the early 1960s through the nationalization of the province's hydroelectric producers.
"Privatizing Hydro-Quebec remains out of the question," Chevrette said.
"Hydro-Quebec must continue to belong to all Quebeckers in contributing to Quebec's economic development," he said.

But Hydro-Quebec, already under government orders to cut its operating costs to generate a greater profit dividend for the province, must become more efficient in face of the deregulation of the North American energy sector, he said.

Opening Hydro-Quebec's power grid would allow private producers in Quebec and other private and public-sector producers in Canada and the United States to reach customers outside Quebec by transporting electricity through the province, the minister said.
Chevrette said the new agency will advise the government on how to reach its new objectives in deregulating Quebec electricity market.

Hydro-Quebec is one of North America's largest electric utilities. It operates generating facilities that have a total capacity of more than 31,000 megawatts, and delivers about 166 billion kilowatthours of electricity each year, of which about 24 billion kilowatthours are exported to neighboring Canadian provinces and the United States.
